persons.name: James Kinzie

occupation.note: 'James Kinzie and family ... resided near Wentworth's tavern' in the list Andreas prints of the settlement's residents; he is a candidate at the 1833 town election and takes five votes. He built the Green Tree Tavern in 1833 and leased it, and he was surety on Mark Beaubien's ferry bond of 6 June 1831.

persons.note: A BUILDER OF TAVERNS RATHER THAN A KEEPER OF THEM, which is why his structure links are thin. Andreas has him building the Green Tree and leasing it to David Clock; Charles Butler in August 1833 lodged at a tavern on the west side of the South Branch 'erected by James Kinzie, but kept by a Mr. Crook (?)' - the question mark is Andreas's or Butler's, not this project's. He is a half-brother to John H. and Robert A. Kinzie. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 3 times: Poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago, 10 August 1833 — “Kinzie, James” (poll_1833_017, line 38); Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Kinzie, James” (tax_1833_061, line 113); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Kinzie, James” (poll_1834_066, line 235). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Kinzie' agrees with the entry's forenames; 4 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). HALF BROTHER, NOT BROTHER, AND THE SOURCE IS AN EDITOR'S NOTE OF 1881. Hurlbut's bracketed note under the American Fur Company's 1821 consignment entry reads “[The late James Kinzie, formerly of Chicago, and half brother of the late John H. Kinzie.]” — the same father and different mothers, which is the form this dataset keeps, because flattening it to ‘brother’ is the move that lets the three Chicago Kinzies collapse into one another. The two men are kinzie_james in hh_kinzie_james and kinzie_john_h in hh_kinzie_john_h, and this project models them as separate households. Read as bk_afc_015 and cited to chicago_antiquities_american_fur_co. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it is an 1881 recollection about 1821, the ladder abstains on it (rung G5), and it moves no grade, no arrival, no placement and no household membership — both men are attested here on other evidence and stay so. THE RELATIONSHIP HAS NOWHERE QUERYABLE TO LIVE: data/residents/index.json's `relationships` vocabulary describes a person's place WITHIN a household and the household record has no field for a kinship BETWEEN two households, so this is prose beside a cited reading rather than a link. That gap is the finding, and it is filed rather than invented around. The Robert A. limb of this record's own earlier sentence — ‘He is a half-brother to John H. and Robert A. Kinzie’ — is older than this reading, Hurlbut does not carry it, and it is neither cited nor upgraded here.

research_note: A HOUSEHOLD WITH A FAMILY IN THE SOURCE AND NO PEOPLE IN THE RECORD. Andreas's list says 'James Kinzie and family' and this parcel writes one person, because naming a wife or counting children on the strength of the word 'family' is the exact move the grade vocabulary forbids. THE HONEST READING OF THIS RECORD is that it stands for at least three or four people and can defend only one. A KINSHIP THIS RECORD NOW CARRIES AND CANNOT LINK: Hurlbut's 1881 bracketed note makes this head the HALF brother of kinzie_john_h in hh_kinzie_john_h (bk_afc_015). It is written onto the person as a cited book_evidence reading because the household schema has no field for a relationship between two households; the schema question is filed, and nothing about either household's position, arrival, trade or membership changes.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
